# REGIME READ — 2026-09-24

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 2 → 3 (one step bearish).** The previous read's first bearish trigger fired. VIX closed at 15.18 on 09-23 (VIX/VIX3M line, engine 2026-09-23T20:45Z) and reads 16.15 on 09-24 (+6.39%, yfinance). Both are above the Stage-3 floor of 15. The cause was the bond market: the 10Y jumped to 5.114%. That is its highest level since 2007 ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-september-23-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-080556640.html), [ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/major-us-stock-indexes-fared-wednesday-9232026-136697299)).
- **Total score: −2 → −5 (delta −3).** Three lenses moved down: Dealer flow 0 → −1, Macro −1 → −2 and Cross-asset +1 → 0. The mix is now 0 bullish, 3 bearish and 4 neutral.
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bullish — NDX ≥ 30,000 with VXN below 19:* **ARMED, and moved further away.** The price leg still holds: NDX is at 30,470.29 (−0.9% from its 52-week high, snapshot). VXN went the wrong way again, to 20.76 (09-23, yfinance). It would now need to fall 8.48%.
  - *Bullish — breadth above 45% of stocks over their 50-day average:* **ARMED, and moving away.** Only 30.4% of S&P 500 stocks were above their 50-day average on 09-22 ([thetrading.tools](https://www.thetrading.tools/market-breadth)). The last broad-universe reading was 31.4% (09-18).
  - *Bullish — a concluded US–China truce extension or tariff reduction:* **FIRED, but only the smaller half.** Bessent announced that the Busan truce now runs two more months, to **Jan 10** ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/world-news/trump-welcomes-xi-jinping-as-us-china-trade-truce-extended-by-2-months-126092400113_1.html), [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-24/trump-xi-buy-time-on-trade-with-neither-able-to-afford-a-fight)). There was no tariff reduction. Bloomberg's headline, "Trump, Xi Buy Time", describes it well: this delays the risk rather than removing it.
  - *Bullish — Brent confirmed below $92:* **ARMED, and moved away.** The snapshot shows Brent at $105.05 (+1.91%, 09-24). AP says oil "halted its slide" ([ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/major-us-stock-indexes-fared-wednesday-9232026-136697299)). See the data note: the size of this jump could not be reconciled.
  - *Bearish — VIX back above 15:* **FIRED.** 15.18 on 09-23, then 16.15 on 09-24.
  - *Bearish — VXN > 22:* **DID NOT FIRE, but it moved closer.** VXN is at 20.76 and would need to rise 5.97% (it needed +9.02% last read).
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **DID NOT FIRE.** NDX would need to fall 6.79%. The nearer 30,000 line is only −1.54% away.
  - *Bearish — 10Y closing above 5.00% on two consecutive sessions:* **HALF-FIRED, still ARMED.** 09-23 closed at **5.114%** (+3.04%, snapshot), the first close above 5% since the 09-18 dispute. One more close at or above 5.00% today (09-24) fires it.
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%:* **DID NOT FIRE.** HY is at 2.68% (+2bp) and IG at 0.77% (flat), both 09-22 (FRED). Credit is still calm.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ below the 4-week low of $66.55:* **DID NOT FIRE.** The 4-week low is now $66.42, and spot is 18.43% above it.
- **Notable lens flips:**
  - **Dealer flow 0 → −1.** VIX broke 15. MOVE (bond-market volatility) jumped +17.55%. SKEW and VVIX both rose.
  - **Macro −1 → −2.** The 10Y reversed from under 5% to a 2007 high in one session.
  - **Cross-asset +1 → 0.** The "Brent below $100" condition behind last read's upgrade is no longer supported by any checked print.

## Regime Stage Tracker
- Current Stage: 3 — Neutral / choppy
- Stage Anchor: 2026-09-23. The 10Y hit 5.114% (a 2007 high) after a strong business-activity report showed costs rising at the fastest pace in years. VIX closed back above 15 the same day ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-september-23-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-080556640.html)).
- Position: Week 1 of an estimated 1–3. This is the first read in Stage 3.
- Confidence: Medium. Four lenses are neutral and three are bearish, with none bullish. That fits a choppy Stage 3, but not 5+ aligned.
- Bullish trigger (-> next bullish stage): all three together:
  - VIX back below 15 (−7.12%).
  - The 10Y back below 5.00% on a close.
  - NDX holding above 30,000.
- Bearish trigger (-> next bearish stage): any one of these:
  - The 10Y closing at or above 5.00% again on 09-24. That makes two consecutive closes.
  - VXN above 22 (+5.97%).
  - NDX closing below 30,000 (−1.54%).
  - VIX above 20 (+23.8%) and rising.
  - HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%.

## Regime Verdict
The bond market has taken over from geopolitics as the main risk. The 10Y reached a 2007 high the same day VIX broke back above 15. This happened while the Nasdaq sits within 1% of its record on thin breadth, so the grind higher has become a choppy, rate-sensitive tape. Medium confidence.

**Data note:** WebSearch was available, so this is a full read with no confidence cap. Six items need care:
1. **Some Day Change figures in the snapshot do not match that single session.**
   - AP has the Nasdaq Composite at **−1.1%** (−308.24 pts) on 09-23, not −0.69% ([ABC/AP](https://abcnews.com/Business/wireStory/major-us-stock-indexes-fared-wednesday-9232026-136697299)).
   - The NDX level of 30,470.29 against last read's 30,732.40 implies about **−0.85%**, not −0.04%.
   - AP has the DJI at **−0.7%** (−352.10 pts), not −1.03%.
   - SPX matches (−0.8%).
   - I copied the table verbatim as instructed. Use the levels and treat the Day Change column with caution.
2. **The Brent feed jumped from $96.16 (last read) to $105.05, but reports only +1.91% for the day.** Those two numbers cannot both be right for one session. The feed may have switched contracts. I could not verify $105 independently. AP says only that oil "halted its slide".
3. **VXN:** the snapshot shows 20.76 and the engine block shows 20.18. The 20.18 figure equals last read's value, so it is probably stale. I use 20.76.
4. **TQQQ day change:** the engine shows −2.50%, but last read's spot of $80.83 to $78.66 implies −2.68%. Last read's $80.83 was never independently confirmed.
5. **CNN Fear & Greed:** one source shows 35 ([finhacker](https://www.finhacker.cz/en/fear-and-greed-index-historical-data-and-chart/)) and another shows 71 ([convextrade](https://convextrade.com/today/fear-and-greed-index)), both for 09-23. I use 35, which matches the prior series and the source used before.
6. **Not retrieved:** AAII, CFTC COT, NAAIM, margin debt, ETF flows, Citi Economic Surprise, insiders and buybacks, Copper/Gold, transports, Bitcoin, and broad-universe breadth after 09-18.

## Diverging Signals
- **Price versus rates.** NDX is only 0.9% below its record, yet the 10Y is at a 2007 high. Mega-cap growth stocks are priced off long-term rates (higher rates make their future profits worth less today). Normally this cannot last: either yields ease or tech valuations give way. On 09-23 the Nasdaq Composite fell about 1.1% on the yield jump, which suggests the market has started to take notice.
- **Stocks and bonds versus credit.** VIX, MOVE, SKEW and VVIX all rose together. Credit spreads did not move (HY 2.68%, IG 0.77%). So the market is repricing rates, not default risk yet. Stage 4 would need credit to join in.
- **Good trade news, bad bond news.** The China truce extension was the bullish trigger the last read was waiting for. It fired and stocks still fell. When good news does not lift the market, it usually means another driver (here, rates) is in charge.
- **Heavy hedging with a stretched index.** TQQQ put/call is 1.73 and SKEW is rising. That protection is being bought close to highs, not after a fall. Once positions are hedged, dips can be shallower. But it also shows traders do not trust the rally.

## TQQQ Read
- **Momentum: neutral, but close to overbought.** RSI(14) is 67.9 (09-23). It is still only about 2 points below the 70 line (where a move is considered stretched), even after a −2.50% day. The five-day green streak ended. For a put seller, the premium is not being lifted by an oversold bounce setup. The risk is a pullback from a stretched level.
- **Market structure: SIDEWAYS.**
  - RALLY fails: spot is 18.43% above the 4-week low of $66.42, and it needs more than 30% (the line is $86.35).
  - DOWNTURN fails on both legs: spot is only 2.84% below the 4-week high of $80.96, not 20%, and VXN is 20.76, below 25.
  - This is the nineteenth consecutive SIDEWAYS read.
- **Trend: uptrend on both horizons.** Spot is 11.17% above the 50DMA ($70.76) and about 25.9% above the 200DMA. Neither is under threat from one day's move. The 50DMA sits just below the bottom of the expected-move band ($71.75).
- **Volatility & premium environment: the seller's cushion shrank for a third read in a row.**
  - IV/HV (20d) fell from 1.18 to **1.11** (HV20 49.5%, daily plan 09-23). Options now cost only about 11% more than the fund has actually been moving.
  - Quoted ATM IV fell to 55% from 57%, even as VXN rose. TQQQ's own options did not reprice with the index's fear gauge.
  - Put demand is heavy (put/call 1.73) and crash-protection pricing is rising (SKEW 146.15). Protection further below spot is likely costlier than at-the-money, so the richer premium sits further down the chain, not at the money.
- **Put-selling context: CAUTIOUS, with HOSTILE one close away.**
  - The rate leg of HOSTILE is half-fired. The 10Y closed at 5.114% on 09-23. One more close at or above 5.00% on 09-24 fires it.
  - The other HOSTILE legs are not close. VXN would need to rise 20.4% to reach 25. Spot is 18.43% above the 4-week low. HY is at 2.68%, well below 3.25%.
  - FAVOURABLE has moved further out of reach. VXN is 20.76, not below 19. Brent is not below $100 on any checked print.
  - For a put seller, the premium cushion is thin, the fund is near its highs with RSI near 70, and the market's biggest driver has become the long-bond yield. That is a backdrop where downside moves can come fast and without a headline.

  This is context only — no strikes, expiries, sizes, or trade calls.

## Forward Levels & Triggers
- Bullish trigger: the 10Y back below 5.00% on a close, VIX back below 15, and NDX holding 30,000. That would return the regime to Stage 2. For TQQQ, a close above $86.35 flips the structure to RALLY.
- Bearish trigger: a second 10Y close at or above 5.00% (09-24); NDX closing below 30,000 (−1.54%); VXN above 22 (+5.97%); or TQQQ closing below the $70.76 50DMA (−10.04%).
- Neutralizer: the remaining days of Xi's visit, which covers AI, rare earths, auto access and Taiwan. A concrete rare-earth or tech-export deal would ease the tariff and tech channel. A Taiwan or export-control clash would reopen it while the Nasdaq is near its record. A breakdown in the US–Iran talks would put the oil channel back in play.

## This Period's Catalysts
- **Trump–Xi summit, Washington** (three-day visit beginning 2026-09-24). The truce is already extended to Jan 10. The open topics are AI, rare earths, auto access and Taiwan.
- **Quarter-end rebalance, 2026-09-30.** After a quarter in which stocks rose and bonds fell, rebalancing funds may need to sell stocks.
- **NFP / jobs report (September data), 2026-10-02, 08:30 ET** (bls.gov, verified 2026-08-29). With the 10Y at 5.11%, a strong report would push yields higher.
- **US–Iran talks:** more sessions are planned after the 09-23 meeting. Trump says he expects a deal after the midterms (2026-11-03).
- Q3 mega-cap earnings season begins mid-to-late October. Exact dates were not retrieved.

## Expiry-Window Flag
- Catalysts inside the next 5 trading days: no scheduled macro or central-bank release was found for 09-24 to 09-30. The Trump–Xi summit (09-24 to 09-26) and quarter-end (09-30) fall inside the window. NFP (10-02) falls just outside it.
- Window: CLEAN-WINDOW — none scheduled (headline/geopolitical risk may still apply). Headline risk is elevated: the summit, the Iran rhetoric, and a bond market that moved sharply on a data release.

## Structural Calendar Flag (deterministic — always report)
- **Quad-witching:** next date is 2026-12-18 (3rd Friday of December), 85 calendar days away. It is not inside 2 sessions.
- **Quarter-end rebalance:** 2026-09-30 (Wednesday), the 5th session counting today (09-24). It is not inside 2 sessions yet, but it will be from Monday 09-28.
- Net: neither is inside 2 sessions today. From 09-28, closing-auction volume and end-of-quarter drift can be larger than normal. Fills near the close may behave differently.
